1 John 1.summary: John and his fellow witnesses declare that which was from the beginning, which they have heard, which they have seen with their eyes, which they have looked upon, and their hands have handled, of the Word of life, for the life was manifested, and they bear witness and shew that eternal life, which was with the Father (1 John 1:1–2). They declare it that others may have fellowship with them, and truly their fellowship is with the Father, and with his Son Jesus Christ, and they write that their joy may be full (1 John 1:3–4). This is the message that God is light, and in him is no darkness at all (1 John 1:5). If we say that we have fellowship with him and walk in darkness, we lie, but if we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have fellowship one with another, and the blood of Jesus Christ his Son cleanseth us from all sin (1 John 1:6–7). If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, but if we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness, and if we say that we have not sinned, we make him a liar (1 John 1:8–10).
1 John 1.whereWeAre: 1 John follows 2 Peter. John writes of the Word of life, which they have heard, seen, and handled, that their joy may be full, and tells how to walk in the light, confessing sin and trusting the blood of Jesus Christ (1:1-10). Chapter 2 gives Christ our advocate, the commandment of love, and a warning about antichrists.

keyFigures.name: John and his fellow witnesses
keyFigures.role: Declare what they have heard, seen with their eyes, and handled of the Word of life (1:1-3).

keyFigures.name: The Word of life, Jesus Christ
keyFigures.role: The life that was manifested, whose blood cleanseth us from all sin (1:1-2,7).

keyFigures.name: God the Father, who is light
keyFigures.role: In him is no darkness at all, and he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins (1:2,5,9).

keyFigures.name: Those who walk in the light or in darkness
keyFigures.role: Those who say they have fellowship with him and either walk in the light or lie (1:6-7).

keyThemes.explanation: The writers have heard, seen, and handled the Word of life, for the life was manifested and they bear witness (1:1-3).
They declare it that others may have fellowship with them, and with the Father and his Son Jesus Christ, that their joy may be full (1:3-4).
God is light, and in him is no darkness at all, so those who walk in the light have fellowship and are cleansed by the blood of Jesus Christ (1:5-7).
If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us and cleanse us, and to say we have not sinned is to make him a liar (1:8-10).

1 John 2.summary: John writes to his little children that they sin not, and if any man sin, we have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous, who is the propitiation for our sins, and not for ours only but also for the sins of the whole world (1 John 2:1–2). Hereby we do know that we know him, if we keep his commandments, and he that saith I know him and keepeth not his commandments is a liar, but whoso keepeth his word, in him is the love of God perfected, and he ought himself so to walk, even as he walked (1 John 2:3–6). It is an old commandment which they had from the beginning, and a new commandment which is true in him and in them, because the darkness is past and the true light now shineth (1 John 2:7–8). He that saith he is in the light and hateth his brother is in darkness, but he that loveth his brother abideth in the light (1 John 2:9–11). He writes to little children, fathers, and young men, because their sins are forgiven, because they have known him from the beginning, and because they have overcome the wicked one (1 John 2:12–14). They are not to love the world, neither the things in the world, for the lust of the flesh, the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life are not of the Father, and the world passeth away, but he that doeth the will of God abideth for ever (1 John 2:15–17). It is the last time, and there are many antichrists, who went out from us because they were not of us, but the believers have an unction from the Holy One (1 John 2:18–21). He is a liar that denieth that Jesus is the Christ, and whosoever denieth the Son hath not the Father, so let that abide in them which they have heard from the beginning, and this is the promise that he hath promised us, eternal life (1 John 2:22–25). The anointing which they have received of him abideth in them, so they are to abide in him, that when he shall appear they may have confidence, and not be ashamed before him at his coming (1 John 2:26–29).
1 John 2.whereWeAre: Chapter 1 ended with confession of sin and a God who is faithful and just to forgive (1:9-10). Chapter 2 names Jesus Christ the righteous as our advocate, links knowing him with keeping his commandments and loving the brethren, and warns against loving the world and against many antichrists (2:1-29). Chapter 3 speaks of the sons of God.

keyFigures.name: Jesus Christ the righteous
keyFigures.role: Our advocate with the Father and the propitiation for the sins of the whole world (2:1-2).

keyFigures.name: The Father
keyFigures.role: In whom the love is perfected in those that keep his word, and whom the antichrist denies (2:5,15,22-23).

keyFigures.name: Little children, fathers, and young men
keyFigures.role: Told that their sins are forgiven, that they have known him, and that they have overcome the wicked one (2:12-14).

keyFigures.name: He that hateth his brother
keyFigures.role: Is in darkness and walketh in darkness (2:9-11).

keyFigures.name: The many antichrists
keyFigures.role: Went out from us because they were not of us and deny that Jesus is the Christ (2:18-22).

keyThemes.explanation: If any man sin we have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous, who is the propitiation for our sins (2:1-2).
We know that we know him if we keep his commandments, and he that saith he abideth in him ought to walk even as he walked (2:3-6).
He that loveth his brother abideth in the light, and he that hateth his brother is in darkness (2:7-11).
They are not to love the world, for the lust of the flesh, the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life pass away, but he that doeth the will of God abideth for ever (2:15-17).

keyThemes.theme: Discernment and remaining in the message
keyThemes.explanation: Many antichrists went out from them, but the anointing from the Holy One abides in believers, who are to continue in the Son and in the Father (2:18-27).

1 John 3.summary: Behold, what manner of love the Father hath bestowed upon us, that we should be called the sons of God, and when he shall appear we shall be like him, for we shall see him as he is, and every man that hath this hope in him purifieth himself, even as he is pure (1 John 3:1–3). Whosoever committeth sin transgresseth also the law, and Christ was manifested to take away our sins, and whosoever abideth in him sinneth not (1 John 3:4–6). He that doeth righteousness is righteous, but he that committeth sin is of the devil, for the Son of God was manifested that he might destroy the works of the devil, and in this the children of God are manifest, and the children of the devil (1 John 3:7–10). This is the message that we should love one another, not as Cain, who was of that wicked one and slew his brother, and we know that we have passed from death unto life because we love the brethren, for whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer (1 John 3:11–15). Hereby perceive we the love of God, because he laid down his life for us, and we ought to lay down our lives for the brethren, and whoso hath this world's good and seeth his brother have need and shutteth up his bowels from him cannot be said to have the love of God dwelling in him (1 John 3:16–17). They are not to love in word, neither in tongue, but in deed and in truth, and hereby they know that they are of the truth and shall assure their hearts before him (1 John 3:18–19). If our heart condemn us, God is greater than our heart and knoweth all things, and if our heart condemn us not, we have confidence toward God and receive whatsoever we ask, because we keep his commandments (1 John 3:20–22). This is his commandment, that we should believe on the name of his Son Jesus Christ and love one another, and he that keepeth his commandments dwelleth in him, and we know that he abideth in us by the Spirit which he hath given us (1 John 3:23–24).
1 John 3.whereWeAre: Chapter 2 ended with abiding in him until he shall appear (2:28-29). Chapter 3 shows the love the Father bestowed in calling us sons of God, contrasts the children of God and of the devil, and calls them to love in deed and in truth (3:1-24). Chapter 4 tells them to try the spirits.

keyFigures.name: The Father
keyFigures.role: Hath bestowed such love that we should be called the sons of God (3:1).

keyFigures.name: Jesus Christ, the Son of God
keyFigures.role: Was manifested to take away our sins and to destroy the works of the devil, and laid down his life for us (3:5,8,16).

keyFigures.name: The children of God
keyFigures.role: Doers of righteousness who love the brethren and have passed from death unto life (3:2,10,14).

keyFigures.name: Cain and his brother
keyFigures.role: Cain was of that wicked one and slew his brother because his works were evil and his brother's righteous (3:12).

keyFigures.name: The devil
keyFigures.role: Sinneth from the beginning, and the children of the devil are manifest (3:8,10).

keyFigures.name: The Spirit
keyFigures.role: Given to us, by whom we know that he abideth in us (3:24).

keyThemes.explanation: Now are we the sons of God, and when he shall appear we shall be like him, and every man that hath this hope in him purifieth himself (3:1-3).
Whosoever abideth in him sinneth not, and he that committeth sin is of the devil, for the Son of God was manifested to destroy the works of the devil (3:4-10).
They are not to be as Cain, who slew his brother, for whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer, and we have passed from death unto life because we love the brethren (3:11-15).
Christ laid down his life for us, so we ought to lay down our lives for the brethren, and to help a brother in need and love in deed and in truth, not in word only (3:16-18).

keyThemes.theme: Assurance and the command to believe and love
keyThemes.explanation: If our heart condemn us, God is greater than our heart, and his commandment is to believe on the name of his Son Jesus Christ and love one another (3:19-24).

1 John 4.summary: Beloved, believe not every spirit, but try the spirits whether they are of God, because many false prophets are gone out into the world (1 John 4:1). Every spirit that confesseth that Jesus Christ is come in the flesh is of God, and every spirit that confesseth not is not of God, and this is that spirit of antichrist (1 John 4:2–3). Little children are of God and have overcome them, because greater is he that is in them than he that is in the world, and hereby we know the spirit of truth and the spirit of error (1 John 4:4–6). Let us love one another, for love is of God, and every one that loveth is born of God, and he that loveth not knoweth not God, for God is love (1 John 4:7–8). In this was manifested the love of God toward us, that God sent his only begotten Son into the world that we might live through him, and herein is love, not that we loved God, but that he loved us and sent his Son to be the propitiation for our sins (1 John 4:9–10). If God so loved us, we ought also to love one another, for no man hath seen God at any time, but if we love one another God dwelleth in us and his love is perfected in us (1 John 4:11–12). We know that we dwell in him because he hath given us of his Spirit, and we have seen and do testify that the Father sent the Son to be the Saviour of the world, and whosoever shall confess that Jesus is the Son of God, God dwelleth in him (1 John 4:13–16). Herein is our love made perfect, that we may have boldness in the day of judgment, for there is no fear in love, but perfect love casteth out fear (1 John 4:17–18). We love him because he first loved us, and if a man say I love God and hateth his brother, he is a liar, for this commandment have we from him, that he who loveth God love his brother also (1 John 4:19–21).
1 John 4.whereWeAre: Chapter 3 ended with the Spirit he hath given us (3:24). Chapter 4 tells them to try the spirits, says God is love and sent his Son, and shows that perfect love casteth out fear and shows itself in love of the brother (4:1-21). Chapter 5 gives the faith that overcometh the world.

keyFigures.name: God
keyFigures.role: Is love, sent his only begotten Son, and loved us first (4:8-10,19).

keyFigures.name: Jesus Christ, the Son of God
keyFigures.role: Come in the flesh, sent to be the propitiation for our sins and the Saviour of the world (4:2,9-10,14).

keyFigures.name: The false prophets
keyFigures.role: Gone out into the world, and their spirit confesseth not that Jesus Christ is come in the flesh (4:1-3).

keyFigures.name: The Spirit of God
keyFigures.role: Given to believers, so they know that they dwell in him (4:2,13).

keyFigures.name: The beloved brethren
keyFigures.role: Told to love one another, and not to say I love God while hating a brother (4:7,11,20-21).

keyFigures.name: The world
keyFigures.role: Those who are of the world, speak of the world, and are overcome by them that are of God (4:4-5).

keyThemes.explanation: They are to try the spirits whether they are of God, and every spirit that confesseth that Jesus Christ is come in the flesh is of God (4:1-6).

keyThemes.theme: God’s love revealed through the Son
keyThemes.explanation: In this was manifested the love of God toward us, that God sent his only begotten Son into the world that we might live through him (4:7-10).
If we love one another, God dwelleth in us and his love is perfected in us, and he that dwelleth in love dwelleth in God (4:11-16).
Perfect love casteth out fear, so believers may have boldness in the day of judgment (4:17-18).

keyThemes.theme: Consistency between loving God and others
keyThemes.explanation: If a man say I love God and hateth his brother, he is a liar, for he that loveth not his brother whom he hath seen cannot love God whom he hath not seen (4:19-21).

1 John 5.summary: Whosoever believeth that Jesus is the Christ is born of God, and this is the love of God, that we keep his commandments, and his commandments are not grievous (1 John 5:1–3). Whatsoever is born of God overcometh the world, and this is the victory that overcometh the world, even our faith, for who is he that overcometh the world but he that believeth that Jesus is the Son of God (1 John 5:4–5). This is he that came by water and blood, even Jesus Christ, and it is the Spirit that beareth witness, and there are three that bear witness in earth, the Spirit, and the water, and the blood, and if we receive the witness of men, the witness of God is greater (1 John 5:6–9). He that believeth on the Son of God hath the witness in himself, and this is the record, that God hath given to us eternal life, and this life is in his Son, so he that hath the Son hath life and he that hath not the Son of God hath not life (1 John 5:10–12). These things are written that they may know that they have eternal life, and this is the confidence that we have in him, that if we ask any thing according to his will, he heareth us (1 John 5:13–15). If any man see his brother sin a sin not unto death, he shall ask and God shall give him life, and all unrighteousness is sin (1 John 5:16–17). Whosoever is born of God sinneth not, but keepeth himself, and that wicked one toucheth him not, and we know that we are of God and the whole world lieth in wickedness (1 John 5:18–19). The Son of God is come and hath given us an understanding that we may know him that is true, and this is the true God and eternal life, and John ends Little children, keep yourselves from idols (1 John 5:20–21).
1 John 5.whereWeAre: Chapter 4 ended with the commandment that he who loveth God love his brother also (4:21). Chapter 5 says the faith that Jesus is the Christ overcometh the world, gives the record of eternal life in the Son, teaches confidence in prayer, and ends with the warning to keep from idols (5:1-21). 2 John follows.

keyFigures.name: Jesus Christ, the Son of God
keyFigures.role: He that came by water and blood, whom whosoever believeth is born of God (5:1,5-6).

keyFigures.name: God the Father
keyFigures.role: Gave the record of his Son and hath given us eternal life in him (5:9-11).

keyFigures.name: The Spirit, the water, and the blood
keyFigures.role: The three that bear witness in earth (5:6-8).

keyFigures.name: Those born of God
keyFigures.role: Overcome the world by faith, keep his commandments, and keep themselves (5:2-4,18).

keyFigures.name: The brother who sinneth
keyFigures.role: One whom a believer may ask life for, if his sin is not unto death (5:16).

keyFigures.name: The wicked one
keyFigures.role: Toucheth not him that is born of God, while the whole world lieth in wickedness (5:18-19).

keyThemes.theme: Faith expressed through love and obedience
keyThemes.explanation: Whosoever believeth that Jesus is the Christ is born of God, and the love of God is that we keep his commandments, which are not grievous (5:1-5).

keyThemes.theme: Testimony about Jesus and life in the Son
keyThemes.explanation: God hath given us eternal life, and this life is in his Son, for he that hath the Son hath life (5:6-12).
These things are written that believers may know that they have eternal life (5:13).
This is the confidence that if we ask any thing according to his will, he heareth us (5:14-17).

keyThemes.theme: Belonging to God and avoiding idols
keyThemes.explanation: Whosoever is born of God sinneth not, and the readers are told Little children, keep yourselves from idols (5:18-21).
